name: Two Receipts, One Year
why_it_works: The cheap fix wins on day one and loses over a year, but people judge on day one. Stacking a year of small repeat charges into one long receipt makes the slow cost feel sudden and physical, which is the only way most people notice it.

hook.pattern: Show two receipts of wildly different length and ask which one was the 'cheap' choice.
examples: One of these receipts was the cheap option. Guess which.
Two ways to handle {{problem}}. Here's what each cost by December.
The short receipt was the expensive choice. Let me explain.

craft.notes: The long receipt is the whole idea: let it physically grow on screen so the cost feels like it piles up. Say the totals out loud only once, in the text-only beat, so the number lands without clutter around it.

do_not: Present illustrative totals as guaranteed savings
Suggest a cheaper option is unsafe unless that is documented
Pack more than one problem into a single ad
compliance: Label all totals as illustrative examples, not quotes or guaranteed savings
Dental and chiropractic: no promises of outcomes or that one visit fixes a condition for good; treatment needs vary by patient and must follow state board advertising rules
Insurance: no savings claims without a documented basis; name the licensed agency and state license number where required, and say coverage varies by policy
